from pathlib import Path
obj = {
  "sample_id":"6600447909494784",

    {"step":1,"file":"decoder/ih264d_sei.c","function":"ih264d_parse_sei_payload","line":1008,"var":"ui4_payload_type","code":"case SEI_FILM_GRAIN_CHARACTERISTICS: i4_status = ih264d_parse_fgc(ps_bitstrm, ps_dec, ui4_payload_size);","role":"source","note":"The SEI payload type selects the film-grain parser, so attacker-controlled SEI bytes reach the vulnerable path."},
    {"step":2,"file":"decoder/ih264d_sei.c","function":"ih264d_parse_fgc","line":775,"var":"u1_film_grain_characteristics_cancel_flag","code":"ps_sei->s_sei_fgc_params.u1_film_grain_characteristics_cancel_flag = (UWORD8) ih264d_get_bit_h264(ps_bitstrm);","role":"intermediate","note":"The parser consumes the first control bit from the bitstream and uses it to decide whether to parse the rest of the film-grain structure."},
    {"step":3,"file":"decoder/ih264d_sei.c","function":"ih264d_parse_fgc","line":778,"var":"u1_film_grain_characteristics_cancel_flag","code":"if(0 == ps_sei->s_sei_fgc_params.u1_film_grain_characteristics_cancel_flag)","role":"intermediate","note":"When the cancel flag is clear, the parser continues into the variable-length field parsing that can overrun the bitstream."},
    {"step":4,"file":"decoder/ih264d_sei.c","function":"ih264d_parse_fgc","line":842,"var":"ps_sei->s_sei_fgc_params.ai4_comp_model_value[c][i][j]","code":"ps_sei->s_sei_fgc_params.ai4_comp_model_value[c][i][j] = (WORD32) ih264d_sev(pu4_bitstrm_ofst, pu4_bitstrm_buf);","role":"intermediate","note":"The nested loops repeatedly read signed Exp-Golomb values from the same bitstream without a payload-size bound check."},
    {"step":5,"file":"decoder/ih264d_bitstrm.c","function":"ih264d_get_bits_h264","line":79,"var":"ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst","code":"if(u4_num_bits) GETBITS(u4_code, ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst, ps_bitstrm->pu4_buffer, u4_num_bits);","role":"root_cause","note":"The bit reader advances based on the requested bit count but does not enforce that the read stays within u4_max_ofst, so malformed SEI data can drive an out-of-bounds read."},
    {"step":6,"file":"decoder/ih264d_bitstrm.h","function":"<global>","line":93,"var":"ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst + bits_to_read","code":"#define CHECK_BITS_SUFFICIENT(ps_bitstrm, bits_to_read) (ps_bitstrm->u4_ofst + bits_to_read <= ps_bitstrm->u4_max_ofst)","role":"sink","note":"The required safety predicate is that the next read must remain within the remaining bitstream size; the vulnerable path violates this bound and triggers the heap-buffer-overflow read."}
  ],

    "propagation":[
